description:
Original report: pl2cl --server memory growth, ~6 GB after ~1400 eval requests (regexp_qr_embed); per-request state accumulates.

CAUGHT LIVE AGAIN s365 — same signature, so the s321 diagnosis is confirmed and
this is REPRODUCIBLE, not a one-off:
  PID 357947  PPID 4455 (systemd --user: REPARENTED, client gone)
  ELAPSED 2245 s (37 min AFTER the suite run had finished and reported)
  RSS 5.79 GB   STAT R   %CPU 99.9
  Spawned during the s365 `--all` run's SOLO phase, i.e. op/cond.t — exactly the
  20k-nested-ternary file the s321 diagnosis named.  Killing it returned ~5 GB.
  It burned a full core for 37 minutes DURING the tail of that same suite run,
  which is precisely the #180 wall-clock-inflation mechanism.

CAUGHT LIVE s321 (first sighting): PID 201568, 4.95 GB, STAT R, reparented.

DIAGNOSIS (unchanged, do NOT go fix the EOF path): _run_server's loop
(pl2cl:215) already does `last unless defined $pkg`, so a closed pipe DOES end
the loop, and state R rules out "blocked on read".  The server is still
TRANSPILING when its requester dies; nothing tells it to abandon the
computation, so it runs on holding multi-GB and only learns at the next
read/write.

CANDIDATE FIXES (unchanged; (c) recommended, (a) needs a policy call):
 (a) per-request alarm() cap — generous (minutes) and LOUD when it fires.
 (b) periodic getppid() — only helps between requests.
 (c) the RUNNER reaps any pl2cl --server it spawned when it exits — smallest
     safe change, pure measurement hygiene.  s365's sighting is a second
     argument for doing (c) now: two of two long suite runs left one behind.

Separately still open: the per-request accumulation that reaches multi-GB over
~1400 requests.

CLOSED s406 (e7d16bf) — the ORIGINAL report (per-request growth), measured and
fixed.  The ORPHAN half was closed earlier (s397a getppid tick + the two
runners' reapers).

MEASUREMENT: a driver speaking the server protocol (200 requests: RSS
43100 -> 47192 kB, perfectly linear) and an in-process loop (600 transpiles of
a 50-char snippet: +8.5 kB each, no plateau; a 1.4 kB source leaks ~150 kB per
transpile — it scales with the parse tree).

CAUSE, found by arena census (Devel::Gladiator in a scratch local::lib):
exactly 2 CODE refs leaked per transpile, both from Pl/Parser2.pm
_seam_lex_assign_fix:
    my $walk;  $walk = sub { … $walk->($_) for @$f };
The closure captures the variable that holds it = a reference cycle perl never
collects, so the CV AND its pad (its share of the form) leak per seam
expression.  __SUB__ (feature current_sub, on under `use v5.30`) recurses
without naming itself.

AFTER: 600 in-process transpiles move RSS by 0 kB; 200 server requests by 16 kB
total.  Guard Pl/t/parser-leak-01.t — the SHAPE (no `my $w; $w = sub {… $w->()
…}` in Pl/, lib/ or pl2cl) and the BEHAVIOUR (300 transpiles < 1 MB; inverse
guard measured 5524 kB with HEAD's Parser2.pm through a shadow @INC).
Emission untouched: corpus-diff IDENTICAL 111 files, emission-ab 18/18 SAME.
subject: pl2cl --server LEAKS AND SPINS after its client dies — caught live s321 at 4.95 GB, state R, reparented to systemd
